accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's foodgrain production estimate for 2024-25 before the final estimate?
o: 357.73 million tonnes in the 2nd Advance Estimate
353.96 million tonnes in the 3rd Advance Estimate
376.56 million tonnes in the 3rd Advance Estimate
283 million tonnes in the 3rd Advance Estimate
accepted.x: The earlier estimate for 2024-25 was 353.96 million tonnes in the 3rd Advance Estimate; the final figure was later revised to 357.73 million tonnes.
accepted.tq: Separate successive estimates of the same agricultural year.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the 2025-26 Second Advance Estimates, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The 2025-26 Second Advance Estimates placed kharif foodgrain production at 1,741.44 lakh tonnes and rabi production at 1,745.13 lakh tonnes.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure crop-season and figure pairing.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The total foodgrain production of India reached which figure in 2025-26 according to the cited estimate?
accepted.x: Total foodgrain production reached 376.56 million tonnes in 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total annual figure from kharif and rabi component estimates.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's foodgrain production increased from 265.05 million tonnes in 2013-14 to approximately which earlier estimate for 2018-19?
accepted.x: Foodgrain production was 265.05 million tonnes in 2013-14 and the 2018-19 3rd Advance Estimate was about 283 million tonnes.
accepted.tq: Track the time sequence and select the estimate associated with the specified year.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the trend in India's foodgrain production from 2019-20 to 2024-25?
o: It fluctuated without any definite direction.
accepted.x: Foodgrain production recorded a steady increase over the period from 2019-20 to 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of a reported time-series trend.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The foodgrain production of Andhra Pradesh was 157.59 lakh tonnes in which year?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh produced 157.59 lakh tonnes of foodgrains in 2017-18.
accepted.tq: Match the exact state production figure with its agricultural year.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh foodgrain production figures in chronological order of the agricultural year:
A. 161.86 lakh tonnes
B. About 151 lakh tonnes
C. 143.31 lakh tonnes
D. 157.59 lakh tonnes
accepted.x: The figures correspond respectively to 2017-18, 2018-19, 2023-24 and 2024-25, giving the sequence D, B, C, A.
accepted.tq: First identify the year attached to each figure, then arrange the years.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Second Advance Estimate for Andhra Pradesh foodgrain production in 2025-26 was:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh foodgrain production was estimated at 190.29 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 17.03%.
accepted.tq: Check both the absolute figure and the associated percentage change.
accepted.sec: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding agricultural and allied sector growth?
accepted.x: Agriculture and allied sector growth was 3.1% in the FY26 advance estimate. FY24 was 2.7%, FY25 was later revised to 4.2%, and Q1 FY27 was 3.6%.
accepted.tq: Separate similar annual and quarterly growth rates.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The revised estimate of agriculture and allied sector growth for FY25 was:
accepted.x: FY25 growth was initially reported as 4.6% but was later revised to 4.2%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an initial estimate from its subsequent revision.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Agriculture and allied sector growth in Q1 FY27 was 3.6%.
2. Agriculture and allied sector growth in FY26 provisional estimates was 3.0%.
3. Agriculture and allied sector growth in FY24 was 4.6%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. FY24 growth was 2.7%, not 4.6%; 4.6% was the initial FY25 estimate.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect year-rate association among closely spaced fiscal years.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Agricultural growth at 2011-12 prices in 2015-16 was approximately:
accepted.x: Agricultural growth in 2015-16 was about 0.7% at 2011-12 prices.
accepted.tq: Preserve the decimal place in a low-growth numerical fact.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following years is correctly identified as a year of negative agricultural growth?
accepted.x: Negative agricultural growth occurred in 2002-03, when drought was a major factor, and also in 2014-15.
accepted.tq: Link the negative-growth year with the stated causal factor.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The average agricultural growth during FY16-FY25 was:
accepted.x: The decadal average agricultural growth for FY16-FY25 was 4.4%, described as the highest ever.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the decadal average from sector-specific growth rates.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the growth rates of livestock and fisheries during FY16-FY25?
accepted.x: Livestock grew at 7.1%, while fishing and aquaculture grew at 8.8% during FY16-FY25.
accepted.tq: Compare sectoral growth rates without reversing the paired figures.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the agricultural growth performance of Plans, consider the following statements:
1. The Third Plan recorded the lowest growth among the listed Plans.
2. The Eighth Plan recorded 4.68% growth, exceeding its 4.1% target.
3. The Eighth Plan was the best-performing Plan for agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Third Plan recorded 0.73%, while the Eighth Plan achieved 4.68% against a 4.1% target and was the best-performing Plan.
accepted.tq: Combine the lowest value, target comparison and overall ranking.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Plan and agricultural growth rate are correctly matched?
accepted.x: The First Plan recorded agricultural growth of 2.71%. The Second, Third, Eighth and Ninth Plan figures were 3.15%, 0.73%, 4.68% and 2.44%, respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each Plan with its specific growth rate rather than relying on broad ranking.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following agricultural growth rates in ascending order:
A. Third Plan
B. First Plan
C. Eighth Plan
D. Second Plan
accepted.x: The rates are 0.73% for the Third Plan, 2.71% for the First Plan, 3.15% for the Second Plan and 4.68% for the Eighth Plan.
accepted.tq: Convert the listed figures into an ascending sequence before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The collapse of agricultural performance during the Third Plan, largely due to droughts, contributed to the beginning of the:
accepted.x: The drought-related collapse during the Third Plan helped set off the Green Revolution.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy or technological response linked to the stated crisis.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about agricultural growth is NOT correct?
o: Crops were the fastest-growing component at 8.8%.
Fishing and aquaculture grew by 8.8% during FY16-FY25.
The world average growth referred to was 2.9%.
accepted.x: Crops grew by only 3.5%; fishing and aquaculture was the fastest-growing listed component at 8.8%, followed by livestock at 7.1%.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the sectoral growth figures.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Agricultural Policy, 2000, targeted agricultural growth of:
accepted.x: The National Agricultural Policy, 2000, set a target of more than 4% annual agricultural growth.
accepted.tq: Recall the policy target rather than the later realised growth rate.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of agriculture in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to approximately:
accepted.x: Agriculture's share in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to about 18% in the current reference period.
accepted.tq: Compare the historical and present shares without confusing share with growth rate.
accepted.sec: Agricultural growth rate - by year, Plan and decade  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following crop–leading state pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Gujarat is the leading state for cotton, followed by Telangana and Maharashtra. Rajasthan leads rapeseed-mustard, Gujarat leads groundnut, and Madhya Pradesh leads soybean.
accepted.tq: Use the crop-wise leader table and identify the swapped state.
accepted.sec: Largest producer state → crop  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which state is identified as the leading producer of pulses, followed by Rajasthan and Maharashtra?
accepted.x: Madhya Pradesh leads in pulse production, followed by Rajasthan and Maharashtra in the cited ranking.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the leading state from other major producing states.
accepted.sec: Largest producer state → crop  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Uttar Pradesh leads in wheat production in the cited ranking.
2. Gujarat leads in cotton production.
3. Madhya Pradesh leads in soybean production rather than Maharashtra.
4. Uttar Pradesh leads in sugarcane production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct according to the cited crop-wise rankings.
accepted.tq: Check each crop separately and reject the common soybean-state confusion.
accepted.sec: Largest producer state → crop  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the description 'Rice Bowl of central India'?
accepted.x: Chhattisgarh is described as the 'Rice Bowl of central India'.
accepted.tq: Match the descriptive agricultural title with the state.
accepted.sec: Largest producer state → crop  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct order of the listed leading states for wheat production?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana
Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan
Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan
Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh
accepted.x: The cited order is Uttar Pradesh, followed by Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana.
accepted.tq: Preserve the ranking order rather than merely identifying the states in the list.
accepted.sec: Largest producer state → crop  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the kharif and rabi paddy yields of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
accepted.x: The kharif paddy yield was 5,612 kg/ha, while the rabi yield was higher at 6,979 kg/ha.
accepted.tq: Check the seasonal labels before comparing the two yields.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh's maize yield, as reported in the cited agricultural statistics, was:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded a maize yield of 6,453 kg per hectare.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the maize figure from the state’s paddy and seasonal paddy figures.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which state is identified as having the highest rice yield in India?
accepted.x: Punjab has the highest rice yield among the states referred to, although Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are also high-yield states.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the highest-yield state from other states described as high-yielding.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rice yields:
1. West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh were identified as below the national average in the cited estimate.
2. Heat, dry spells and unseasonal rain were cited among the reasons for lower yields in major rice states.
3. Punjab's high rice yield is associated with canal and tubewell irrigation despite low rainfall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The cited explanation links lower yields in major rice states with climatic stresses, while Punjab benefits from canal and tubewell irrigation despite low rainfall.
accepted.tq: Combine the distributional fact with its environmental and irrigation explanations.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's rice yield of about 2,929 kg per hectare is best compared with China's rice yield of approximately:
accepted.x: India's rice yield was about 2,929 kg/ha, compared with approximately 7,100 kg/ha in China.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the China comparison from the separate global foodgrain average.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the comparison of India's foodgrain yield with the global average?
accepted.x: The cited comparison gives India's foodgrain yield as 2,929 kg/ha against a global average of 4,000 kg/ha.
accepted.tq: Keep the rice-specific China comparison separate from the overall foodgrain world comparison.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's cotton yield of about 440 kg per hectare is approximately how much below the global average of 770 kg per hectare?
accepted.x: The difference is approximately 770 minus 440, or 330 kg per hectare.
accepted.tq: Apply direct subtraction to the two stated yield figures.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bt cotton raised cotton yield from approximately 190 kg per hectare in 2002 to approximately what level in 2023?
accepted.x: Bt cotton was associated with an increase in yield from 190 kg/ha in 2002 to 480 kg/ha in 2023.
accepted.tq: Track the before-and-after values and avoid confusing the target with the achieved yield.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kapas Kanti mission has a target of raising cotton yield to:
accepted.x: The Kapas Kanti mission targets a cotton yield of 755 kg per hectare.
accepted.tq: Separate a future mission target from the present Indian and global averages.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which states are specifically associated with the highest pulse yields in the cited comparison?
accepted.x: Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat have the highest pulse yields, helped by black or semi-arid soils and high seed replacement rates.
accepted.tq: Link the yield ranking with the stated soil and seed-replacement factors.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Oilseed yield in 2024-25 was reported as:
accepted.x: Oilseed yield was 1,398 kg per hectare in 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the oilseed yield figure from the pulse, cotton and rice figures.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Telangana's cultivated area increased from 1.31 crore acres in 2014 to approximately what level in FY23?
accepted.x: Telangana's cultivated area increased from 1.31 crore acres in 2014 to 2.2 crore acres in FY23.
accepted.tq: Compare the initial and later area figures and retain the stated unit.
accepted.sec: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The expansion of cultivated area in Telangana from 2014 to FY23 was associated with:
o: National Agricultural Policy and Mission Indradhanush
accepted.x: The increase in Telangana's cultivated area was associated with the Kaleshwaram project and Mission Kakatiya.
accepted.tq: Identify the infrastructure and programme pair linked to the stated agricultural change.
